# ANSI X3.113-1987 Full BASIC conformance claims

<!-- Generated by Compliance/tools/gen_compliance.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Interpreter under test: **FullBASIC v4**. Reference: ANSI X3.113-1987 (FIPS PUB 68-2).

> **Only claims whose tests pass are listed.** A claim appears here when it is marked `claimed` and every test it cites passes in `results/fullbasic.json`. Known failures (`open` claims) and claims without a passing result are not listed, so absence from this document is not a statement of conformance either way.

Claims listed: **1270**. Known open (not listed): 0. Pending, without a passing test yet (not listed): 12. Not listed for lack of a passing result: 0.

## 1. Scope

This document records the conformance claims of the **FullBASIC v4** interpreter against **ANSI X3.113-1987 (FIPS PUB 68-2)**. The implementation claims the modules defined by §2 (l.470-503):

- **Core** (§4-§12),
- **Enhanced Files** (§11, organizations INTERNAL and NATIVE),
- **Graphics** (§13),
- **Fixed Decimal** (§15).

**Section 14 (Real Time) is not claimed**: it is optional in the standard and is not implemented (claim A-14-01, section 7). **Section 16 (Editing) is not claimed as a module**: the interpreter does not accept the §16 editing commands as program text; the host application's own source editor provides the editing functionality instead (claim A-16-01, section 7).

| 6.5.5 | A-6.5.5-EXC | exception | core | Storing into a string variable a value longer than its maximum length raises fatal exception 1106 (string overflow), which a handler can intercept; a LET into a substring that overflows keeps 1106, while READ, INPUT and file reads into a substring use their own codes (E-1053, E-1054, E-1105). | STR-0045, SEG-0360 |
| 6.6.2 | A-6.6.2-01 | syntax | core | A COLLATE option must sit on a line numbered lower than every string expression or string declaration of the same program unit. | STR-0046 |
| 6.6.2 | A-6.6.2-02 | syntax | core | A program unit may contain at most one COLLATE option. | STR-0047 |
| 6.6.2 | A-6.6.2-03 | syntax | core | A simple string variable may be declared only once per program unit, and a parameter may not appear in a declare statement. | STR-0048, STR-0049 |
| 6.6.2 | A-ECMA-14 | syntax | core | The ECMA examples 'COLLATE NATIVE' and 'STRING*8 last_name$*20, ...' (6.6.3 examples 1 and 3) are fragments: the first is the option of OPTION COLLATE NATIVE and the second is the body of a DECLARE STRING statement (ANSI 6.6.2 prod. 1-6). The full statements are accepted (MAXLEN 20, 8, 8); the fragments written as stand-alone statements are rejected, which is conforming. | ECMA-0017, ECMA-0018, ECMA-0246, ECMA-0247 |
| 6.6.3 | A-6.6.3-EX | syntax | core | The examples of section 6.6.3 show a COLLATE option and a STRING declaration with per-variable length limits. | STR-0050 |
| 6.6.4 | A-6.6.4-01 | semantics | core | COLLATE NATIVE selects the host system's own character ordering; COLLATE STANDARD selects the ordering of Table 8. | STR-0051, STR-0052 |
| 6.6.4 | A-6.6.4-02 | semantics | core | Without a COLLATE option, a program unit uses the STANDARD collating sequence. | STR-0053 |
| 6.6.4 | A-6.6.4-03 | semantics | core | The default maximum string length is implementation-defined but must be at least 132 characters. | STR-0054 |
| 6.6.4 | A-6.6.4-04 | semantics | core | A length-max of zero in a STRING declaration caps that variable at the empty string. | STR-0055 |
| 7.1.1 | A-7.1.1-01 | semantics | core | When no OPTION BASE is given, an array dimension declared with only an upper bound starts at subscript one; OPTION BASE 0 or 1 changes that default for the program unit. | ARR-0116, ARR-0117, ARR-0118 |
| 7.1.1 | A-7.1.1-02 | syntax | core | Every array declaration must write the upper bound of each dimension explicitly. | ARR-0119 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-01 | syntax | core | An array declaration with more than three dimensions, or with an explicit lower bound greater than its upper bound, is rejected before the program runs, even if the declaration is skipped. | ARR-0107, ARR-0108, ARR-0109, ARR-0197 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-02 | syntax | core | A reference to an array element whose number of subscripts differs from the dimensions in the array's declaration is rejected before the program runs, even if the statement would never be executed. | ARR-0110, ARR-0111, ARR-0112, ARR-0198, ARR-0199, ARR-0200 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-03 | syntax | core | A formal array of a function, subprogram, program or picture must not also be named in a DIM or DECLARE statement. | ARR-0120 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-04 | syntax | core | An array that is not a formal parameter is declared exactly once per program unit; a second DIM or DECLARE for the same array is rejected before the program runs. | ARR-0121 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-05 | syntax | core | An array that is not a formal parameter must be declared on an earlier line than any reference to it or to its elements. | ARR-0122 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-06 | syntax | core | A declaration that gives only an upper bound below the default lower bound is rejected, for example DIM A(0) under the default base of one. | ARR-0123 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-07 | syntax | core | An OPTION BASE must sit on an earlier line than every array declaration and every MAT statement using CON, IDN, ZER or NUL$ in the same program unit. | ARR-0124, ARR-0125 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-08 | syntax | core | A program unit may contain at most one OPTION BASE. | ARR-0126 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-TR103 | syntax | core | The main program and its internal routines are one program unit for array declarations: an array dimensioned inside an internal SUB or FUNCTION can be used by the main and by later routines; a reference on a line below its DIM, in the main or in any routine, is rejected before the program runs; and dimensioning the same array twice in the unit (main and routine, or two routines) is rejected. | ARR-0296, ARR-0297, ARR-0298, ARR-0299 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-TR109 | syntax | core | An internal routine (SUB, FUNCTION or PICTURE) is part of its program unit, which is the main program or an EXTERNAL unit: an array that the routine declares with DECLARE NUMERIC or DECLARE STRING, or dimensions with DIM in an internal PICTURE, can be used by the main and by later routines; a DIM in an internal routine of an EXTERNAL unit can be used by the body of that unit and by its other routines; and dimensioning or declaring the same array twice in the unit (body and routine, two routines, main and PICTURE), or using it on a line below the DIM, is rejected before the program runs. | ARR-0304, ARR-0305, ARR-0306, ARR-0307, ARR-0308, ARR-0309, ARR-0310 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-TR137 | semantics | core | DECLARE NUMERIC and DECLARE STRING of arrays (with or without a lower bound) written inside an internal or an EXTERNAL picture-def declare the array for the program-unit of the picture, in lower-numbered lines than its use: the array of an internal picture is visible to the containing unit; a use in a line lower than the declare-statement is rejected. | ARR-0364, ARR-0365, ARR-0366 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-TR139 | semantics | core | A DIM written inside a FOR, a DO or a multi-line IF (nested to any depth) of an internal SUB, FUNCTION or PICTURE is a declaration of the program unit that contains the routine, exactly like a DIM at the top level of the routine: the array can be used by the containing unit (the main program or the EXTERNAL unit) and by later routines on lines below the DIM, it exists whether or not the DIM is reached, and dimensioning the same array twice in the unit is still rejected. | ARR-0360, ARR-0361, ARR-0362, ARR-0363, ARR-0380, ARR-0381, ARR-0382, ARR-0383, ARR-0384, ARR-0385, ARR-0386 |
| 7.1.2 | A-7.1.2-TR145 | semantics | core | A DIM written in the body of an EXTERNAL SUB, FUNCTION or PICTURE, or in the handler of an EXTERNAL SUB, at any nesting depth, declares the array of that unit whether or not execution reaches it (a branch not taken, a GOTO that jumps over it); a use in a line lower than the DIM, or a second DIM of the same array in the unit, is still rejected. | ARR-0390, ARR-0391, ARR-0392, ARR-0393, ARR-0394, ARR-0395, ARR-0396 |
| 7.1.2 | A-ECMA-15 | syntax | core | DIM with explicit bounds and the SIZE, LBOUND and UBOUND inquiries behave as written. The ECMA example 'A$(3 TO 21) * 8' (7.1.3 example 10) is the body of a DECLARE STRING statement, not of DIM (ANSI 7.1.2 prod. 8 and 10: the length-max belongs to the string-declaration): DECLARE STRING A$(3 TO 21) * 8 is accepted (MAXLEN 8, bounds 3 and 21) and DIM A$(3 TO 21) * 8 is rejected, which is conforming. | ECMA-0019, ECMA-0020, ECMA-0248 |
| 7.1.3 | A-7.1.3-01 | syntax | core | Every declaration and inquiry form shown in the examples of section 7.1.3 is accepted and gives the values the section implies. | ARR-0127 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-01 | semantics | core | After MAT A = ZER(3) on an array declared with ten elements, MAXSIZE(A) is still ten and SIZE(A) is three. | ARR-0101 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-02 | semantics | core | MAXSIZE of an array resized by MAT READ is the size given in its declaration. | ARR-0102 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-03 | semantics | core | MAXSIZE of an array resized by MAT INPUT is the size given in its declaration. | ARR-0103 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-04 | semantics | core | MAXSIZE of an array that receives a smaller array by MAT A = B is the size given in its declaration. | ARR-0104 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-05 | semantics | core | MAXSIZE of an array received as a parameter is the size given in the declaration of the actual array, even after a resize. | ARR-0105 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-06 | semantics | core | MAXSIZE of an array that was never resized is the product of its declared dimension sizes. | ARR-0106 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-07 | syntax | core | LBOUND or UBOUND called with a single argument that names an array of more than one dimension is rejected before the program runs, even if the call would never be executed. | ARR-0113, ARR-0114, ARR-0115 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-08 | semantics | core | The number of bound ranges in a declaration sets the dimension count and each range sets the lowest and highest subscript of its dimension, so DIM D(1980 TO 1989) gives LBOUND 1980 and UBOUND 1989. | ARR-0128 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-09 | semantics | core | An OPTION BASE affects only the program unit that contains it; an external routine keeps its own default lower bound. | ARR-0129 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-10 | semantics | core | Reaching a DIM statement while running has no effect other than moving on to the next line. | ARR-0130 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-11 | semantics | core | A length limit written for a string array in a declaration caps every element; without one the limit of the declared string type applies. | ARR-0131 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-12 | semantics | core | SIZE(A, N) is the current number of subscript values of dimension N, counted from the left starting at one, with N rounded to the nearest integer. | ARR-0132 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-13 | semantics | core | SIZE of a vector is its current element count, including after the vector has been resized by a MAT assignment. | ARR-0101, ARR-0104 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-14 | semantics | core | SIZE of an array with two or three dimensions is the product of its current dimension sizes. | ARR-0133 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-15 | semantics | core | LBOUND(A, N) is the current smallest subscript of dimension N, with N rounded to the nearest integer and counted from the left starting at one. | ARR-0134 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-16 | semantics | core | UBOUND(A, N) is the current largest subscript of dimension N, with N rounded to the nearest integer and counted from the left starting at one. | ARR-0135 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-17 | semantics | core | LBOUND and UBOUND given a vector and no index return the lowest and highest subscript of that vector. | ARR-0136 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-18 | semantics | core | An OPTION BASE in an external SUB, FUNCTION or PICTURE sets the lower bound of the arrays of that unit only; the arrays of the main program keep the default lower bound of one, whether declared before or after the call. | ARR-0204 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-TR117 | semantics | core | A DIM or a DECLARE NUMERIC/STRING with bounds in an internal routine of an EXTERNAL unit creates its array whether or not the routine is ever called (reaching the DIM has no further effect), in every invocation of the unit, and that array is distinct from an array of the same name in the main program or in another unit. | ARR-0314, ARR-0315 |
| 7.1.4 | A-7.1.4-TR135 | semantics | core | Reaching a line that contains a DIM again (a loop or a backward GOTO in an EXTERNAL SUB or FUNCTION, numeric or string, one to three dimensions; or the DIM of a detached-handler, in the main program or in an EXTERNAL unit) has no effect beyond the first time: the array is not created again and keeps the values already assigned. | ARR-0350, ARR-0351, ARR-0352, ARR-0353, ARR-0354 |
| 7.1.5 | E-4004 | exception | core | SIZE with an index below one or above the array's dimension count raises exception 4004, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0138 |
| 7.1.5 | E-4008 | exception | core | LBOUND with an index below one or above the array's dimension count raises exception 4008, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0139 |
| 7.1.5 | E-4009 | exception | core | UBOUND with an index below one or above the array's dimension count raises exception 4009, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0140 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-01 | syntax | core | A redimension list attached to CON, IDN or ZER holds one, two or three bounds. | ARR-0141, ARR-0142 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-02 | syntax | core | In a MAT assignment, the target array and the array expression must have the same number of dimensions; a mismatch is rejected before the program runs. | ARR-0143 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-03 | syntax | core | Both arguments of DOT must be one-dimensional. | ARR-0144 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-04 | syntax | core | IDN accepts at most two redimension bounds. | ARR-0145 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-05 | syntax | core | The two operands of a MAT sum or difference must have the same number of dimensions. | ARR-0146 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-06 | syntax | core | The argument of DET, INV or TRN must be a two-dimensional array; a vector argument is reported when the operation executes — 6002 for DET, 6003 for INV, a nonzero exception code for TRN (ARR-0147). The rule is not checked at load time. | ARR-0147 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-07 | syntax | core | The operands of a MAT product each have one or two dimensions, and at least one of them has two. | ARR-0148 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-TR106 | syntax | core | When the dimensionality of the target array is known at load, a numeric MAT assignment of IDN (with or without redim: the value of IDN, IDN(n) and IDN(n,n) is a matrix) to an array that is not two-dimensional is rejected before the program runs; IDN on a two-dimensional array is valid (that it be square stays a run-time check, 6004). | ARR-0301, ARR-0302, ARR-0303 |
| 7.2.2 | A-7.2.2-TR94 | syntax | core | When the dimensionality of the target array is known at load (DIM, DECLARE, formal array, or a DIM of the containing program for an internal routine), a numeric MAT assignment of CON or ZER whose redim has a different number of redim-bounds than the array (also with a scalar factor, and inside internal routines) is rejected before the program runs; a redim with the same number of dimensions is valid. | ARR-0235, ARR-0236, ARR-0237, ARR-0238, ARR-0239, ARR-0245 |
| 7.2.2 | A-ECMA-16 | semantics | core | MAT assignment, sums, differences, products, scalar-free ZER, INV, TRN, DET and DOT evaluate as written; a bare scalar factor W in a MAT product (MAT A = W * B) is valid and multiplies every element (7.2.3 l.3184, 7.2.4.2 l.3244-3246). | ECMA-0021, ECMA-0022, ECMA-0040 |
| 7.2.3 | A-7.2.3-01 | syntax | core | Every MAT statement and function reference shown in the examples of section 7.2.3 is accepted and computes the value its form implies. | ARR-0149, ARR-0150 |
| 7.2.4.1 | A-7.2.4.1-01 | semantics | core | MAT A = expression evaluates the array expression and stores its elements in A. | ARR-0151 |
| 7.2.4.1 | A-7.2.4.1-02 | semantics | core | After MAT A = B, a vector A has the size of B, even when A was declared larger. | ARR-0104 |
| 7.2.4.1 | A-7.2.4.1-03 | semantics | core | A resized array keeps its lower bounds and its new upper bound is the lower bound plus the new size minus one. | ARR-0152 |
| 7.2.4.1 | A-7.2.4.1-04 | semantics | core | A resize may make one dimension larger than it was declared, as long as the total element count stays within the declared total. | ARR-0153 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-01 | semantics | core | The operators plus and minus on same-sized arrays work element by element, and asterisk is matrix multiplication. | ARR-0154 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-02 | semantics | core | Multiplying an L by M matrix by an M by N matrix gives an L by N matrix of the usual row-by-column sums. | ARR-0155 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-03 | semantics | core | Multiplying a vector of M elements by an M by N matrix gives a vector of N elements. | ARR-0156 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-04 | semantics | core | Multiplying an L by M matrix by a vector of M elements gives a vector of L elements. | ARR-0157 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-05 | semantics | core | Every element of each operand takes part in a MAT expression and each operand is used as a whole, so MAT A = A*B reads the old values of A throughout. | ARR-0158 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-06 | semantics | core | In MAT A = W*B the scalar W is evaluated first and every element of B is multiplied by it. | ARR-0159 |
| 7.2.4.2 | A-7.2.4.2-07 | semantics | core | An underflow inside a MAT expression produces zero for that element and does not stop the program. | ARR-0160 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-01 | semantics | core | CON, IDN or ZER without a redimension list produce an array of the same size as the target. | ARR-0161 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-02 | semantics | core | MAT A = ZER(n) leaves A with exactly n elements, even when A was declared with more. | ARR-0101 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-03 | semantics | core | A single redimension index is the upper bound with the current default lower bound; an index pair joined by TO gives both bounds of the array-value, while the destination array keeps its old lower bound and gets upper = lower + size - 1 (7.2.4.1). | ARR-0162, ARR-0163, ARR-0201, ARR-0202 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-04 | semantics | core | ZER produces an array whose elements are all zero. | ARR-0164 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-05 | semantics | core | CON produces an array whose elements are all one. | ARR-0165 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-06 | semantics | core | IDN produces an identity matrix: ones along the main diagonal, zeros in every other position. | ARR-0166 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-07 | semantics | core | IDN with a redimension always yields a square matrix, and one bound given to IDN acts as if it were given twice. | ARR-0167 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-08 | semantics | core | A scalar multiplier before CON, IDN or ZER replaces every nonzero element by the value of that multiplier. | ARR-0168 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-09 | semantics | core | IDN, TRN, INV and DET operate on the actual bounds of the array: with OPTION BASE 0 the main diagonal of IDN is (0,0), (1,1), ... and TRN/INV/DET read every element within the real limits (7.1.4). | ARR-0203 |
| 7.2.4.3 | A-7.2.4.3-TR178 | semantics | core | The redim-bounds of CON, IDN, ZER and NUL$ are indices and are rounded with INT(X+.5) like those of MAT READ and MAT INPUT: ZER(2.5), CON(1.4 TO 2.6), IDN(2.5), ZER(1.6, 2.4), NUL$(2.5) and 2 * CON(2.5) redimension to the sizes of ZER(3), CON(1 TO 3), IDN(3), ZER(2, 2), NUL$(3) and 2 * CON(3). The bounds are checked after the rounding: ZER(.4) has an upper bound 0 below the default lower bound and CON(1.5 TO .6) has bounds 2 and 1, both 6005, while ZER(.5) has upper bound 1. | ARR-0397, ARR-0398 |
| 7.2.4.4 | A-7.2.4.4-01 | semantics | core | TRN returns the transpose: an M by N argument gives an N by M result. | ARR-0169 |
| 7.2.4.4 | A-7.2.4.4-02 | semantics | core | INV returns the inverse of a square matrix. | ARR-0170 |
| 7.2.4.4 | A-7.2.4.4-03 | semantics | core | DET returns the determinant of a square matrix. | ARR-0171 |
| 7.2.4.4 | A-7.2.4.4-04 | semantics | core | DOT(X, Y) is the scalar inner product of two vectors. | ARR-0172 |
| 7.2.5 | E-1005 | exception | core | An overflow while evaluating a numeric array expression (sum, matrix product or scalar times array) raises exception 1005, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0031, ARR-0032, ARR-0033 |
| 7.2.5 | E-1005-F | exception | fixed | Under ARITHMETIC FIXED, exceeding the maximum precision while evaluating a numeric array expression also raises exception 1005. | ARR-0036 |
| 7.2.5 | E-1009 | exception | core | An overflow while evaluating DET or DOT raises exception 1009, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0034, ARR-0035 |
| 7.2.5 | E-3009 | exception | core | INV of a singular matrix, or a loss of all significant digits while inverting, raises exception 3009, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0179 |
| 7.2.5 | E-5001 | exception | core | A resize that needs more elements than the array's declaration reserved raises exception 5001, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0174 |
| 7.2.5 | E-6001 | exception | core | A numeric array expression whose operand sizes do not fit the rules of matrix algebra raises exception 6001, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0173 |
| 7.2.5 | E-6002 | exception | core | DET of a non-square matrix raises exception 6002, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0177 |
| 7.2.5 | E-6003 | exception | core | INV of a non-square matrix raises exception 6003, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0178 |
| 7.2.5 | E-6004 | exception | core | IDN with a non-square redimension, or assigned to a non-square target when no redimension is given, raises exception 6004, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0176 |
| 7.2.5 | E-6005 | exception | core | A redimension whose first index exceeds the second, or whose single index is below the default lower bound, raises exception 6005, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0175 |
| 7.3.2 | A-7.3.2-01 | syntax | core | In a string MAT assignment, the target array and the array expression must have the same number of dimensions. | ARR-0181 |
| 7.3.2 | A-7.3.2-02 | syntax | core | Two string arrays that are concatenated must have the same number of dimensions. | ARR-0182 |
| 7.3.2 | A-7.3.2-TR89 | syntax | core | When the dimensionality of the string arrays involved is known at load (DIM or DECLARE), a string MAT assignment between arrays of different numbers of dimensions, and a concatenation of two string arrays of different numbers of dimensions, are rejected before the program runs; the mismatch in SIZE between arrays of the same dimensionality is still the run-time exception 6101. | ARR-0231, ARR-0232, ARR-0233, ARR-0234 |
| 7.3.2 | A-7.3.2-TR94 | syntax | core | When the dimensionality of the target string array is known at load, an assignment of NUL$ whose redim has a different number of redim-bounds than the array is rejected before the program runs. | ARR-0240, ARR-0241 |
| 7.3.2 | A-ECMA-17 | semantics | core | MAT string assignment with concatenation, NUL$ and a parenthesised literal prefix fills every element as written. | ECMA-0023 |
| 7.3.3 | A-7.3.3-01 | syntax | core | Every string MAT statement shown in the examples of section 7.3.3 is accepted and produces the array its form implies. | ARR-0183 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-01 | semantics | core | MAT A$ = expression evaluates the string array expression and stores its elements in A$. | ARR-0184 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-02 | semantics | core | A string array target is resized to the shape of the value and keeps its number of dimensions. | ARR-0185 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-03 | semantics | core | A resized string array keeps its lower bounds and its new upper bound is the lower bound plus the new size minus one. | ARR-0186 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-04 | semantics | core | When the target of a string MAT assignment has a substring qualifier, each element has only the selected part replaced. | ARR-0187 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-05 | semantics | core | The substring qualifier on the target is evaluated before the right-hand array expression. | ARR-0188 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-06 | semantics | core | Concatenating two string arrays joins corresponding elements, and the arrays must have equal size in every dimension. | ARR-0189 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-07 | semantics | core | Concatenating a scalar string with an array puts the scalar in front of, or behind, every element. | ARR-0190 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-08 | semantics | core | A substring qualifier on an array operand extracts that substring from every element. | ARR-0191 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-09 | semantics | core | A string MAT assignment is carried out in four steps: target qualifiers, then operand subscripts, qualifiers and values from left to right, then concatenation, then assignment. | ARR-0192 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-10 | semantics | core | NUL$ makes an array of empty strings sized by its redimension list, or like the target when there is none, and follows the same redimension rules as the numeric constants. | ARR-0193 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-71 | semantics | core | A string-array-value of the form string-primary & NUL$ (7.3.2 production 5) prefixes the scalar to every element of the generated null-string array, with or without a redim and whatever the string-primary (literal, variable, expression); the example of 7.3.3 (MAT A$ = ("Number") & B$ after MAT B$ = ("b") & NUL$) gives "Num bb" in every element. | ARR-0295 |
| 7.3.4 | A-7.3.4-72 | semantics | core | A substring-qualifier applied to a string-array operand of a concatenation (7.3.2 productions 3 and 4) extracts that substring from each element of the array before the concatenation, whichever operand carries it: MAT A$ = B$(2:3) & "x" gives "bcx efx hix" for B$ = abc, def, ghi, and the qualifier works on the left, the right or both operands of a concatenation of two arrays. | ARR-0300 |
| 7.3.5 | A-7.3.5-CL36 | semantics | core | The declared length-max of a string-array holds for a MAT with a substring-qualifier on the left and for an array passed by reference to an EXTERNAL SUB. MAT S$(2:1) = ("Z") & NUL$ on elements "ab" of a STRING*2 array and MAT S$(1:0) = ("xyz") & NUL$ raise 1106 and leave the array unchanged, while a replacement that fits works. An EXTERNAL SUB assigning an element longer than the length-max of the argument raises 1106 with LET (EXTYPE 101106 in the caller) and 1053 with READ (101053), as an internal SUB does. | ARR-0400 |
| 7.3.5 | E-1106 | exception | core | Storing a string longer than the allowed maximum, in a string array element or as the value of a string function, raises exception 1106, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0196, ARR-0195 |
| 7.3.5 | E-6101 | exception | core | A string array expression whose operands differ in size raises exception 6101, which a handler can intercept. | ARR-0194 |
| 8.1.2 | A-ECMA-18 | semantics | core | Logical expressions with NOT, AND, OR and comparisons evaluate with the standard precedence; NOT also works at the start of an IF condition. | ECMA-0024 |
| 8.1.3 | A-8.1.3-EX | syntax | core | Every relational-expression example of section 8.1.3 is accepted and evaluates as written. | CTL-0007 |
| 8.1.4 | A-8.1.4-01 | semantics | core | Two numeric expressions compare equal exactly when they have the same value. | CTL-0008 |
| 8.1.4 | A-8.1.4-02 | semantics | core | Two string expressions compare equal exactly when their values have the same length and identical character sequences. | CTL-0009 |
| 8.1.4 | A-8.1.4-03 | semantics | core | String ordering follows the collating sequence: for equal lengths the leftmost differing character decides; a shorter string that is empty or a left prefix of the other compares lower; for other unequal lengths the shorter string is compared against the same-length leftmost part of the longer one, and the remaining relations derive from this less-than rule. | CTL-0010 |
| 8.1.4 | A-8.1.4-04 | semantics | core | NOT applies only to the relational-primary right after it, AND to the relational-terms on both of its sides, and OR to the conjunctions on both of its sides, as the grammar implies. | CTL-0011 |
| 8.1.4 | A-8.1.4-05 | semantics | core | A relational expression short-circuits: its conjunctions are tried left to right and the first true one makes the whole disjunction true with the rest skipped; inside a conjunction the terms are tried left to right and the first false one makes the conjunction false with the rest skipped. | CTL-0012 |
| 8.1.4 | A-8.1.4-06 | semantics | core | A relational-term takes the truth value of its relational-primary, inverted when NOT is present, and a parenthesized relational expression is evaluated by applying these same rules again. | CTL-0013 |
| 8.2.2 | A-ECMA-19 | semantics | core | GO TO, GOTO, ON...GO TO with ELSE, GO SUB, GOSUB and ON...GOSUB with ELSE transfer control as written. | ECMA-0025, ECMA-0026, ECMA-0027, ECMA-0028 |
| 8.2.3 | A-8.2.3-EX | syntax | core | Every control-transfer example of section 8.2.3 is accepted and behaves as written. | CTL-0014, CTL-0015, CTL-0016 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-01 | semantics | core | GOTO moves execution to the line whose number it names. | CTL-0017 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-02 | semantics | core | ON GOTO evaluates its index, rounds it to an integer, and picks the line at that 1-based position in the list; if the index is below 1 or beyond the list and an ELSE clause exists, the statement after ELSE runs and, when it does not jump elsewhere, execution continues with the next line. | CTL-0018 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-03 | semantics | core | Each GOSUB pushes the line number of the GOSUB line itself onto the return stack and then jumps to the target line. | CTL-0019 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-04 | semantics | core | ON GOSUB rounds its index to pick a 1-based list entry, pushes its own line number onto the stack of the enclosing unit or internal procedure, and jumps there; an out-of-range index with an ELSE runs the ELSE statement without altering the stack, and if that statement does not jump, execution continues with the next line. | CTL-0020 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-05 | semantics | core | RETURN removes the top line number from the stack and resumes at the line after the one holding that number. | CTL-0021 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-06 | semantics | core | Inside an internal procedure, GOSUB, ON GOSUB and RETURN work only with that procedure's own stack; elsewhere they work with the stack of the containing program unit. | CTL-0022 |
| 8.2.4 | A-8.2.4-07 | semantics | core | The return stack of a program unit or internal procedure is discarded when that unit or procedure ends, even if GOSUBs were left unmatched; END SUB / EXIT SUB / END FUNCTION / EXIT FUNCTION with a pending GOSUB do not act as RETURN. | CTL-0023, CTL-0059, CTL-0060, CTL-0061, CTL-0062, CTL-0063, CTL-0064, CTL-0065 |
| 8.2.5 | E-10001 | exception | core | ON GOTO or ON GOSUB without an ELSE whose rounded index is below 1 or beyond the list raises the fatal exception 10001. | CTL-0024 |
| 8.2.5 | E-10002 | exception | core | A RETURN executed with no earlier GOSUB or ON GOSUB in the same program unit or internal procedure raises the fatal exception 10002. | CTL-0025, CTL-0026 |
| 8.3.2 | A-8.3.2-01 | syntax | core | EXIT DO is only valid inside a DO loop and EXIT FOR only inside a FOR loop, so a program with either outside its loop is rejected before it runs, even if the statement would never be executed. | CTL-0001, CTL-0002, CTL-0003, CTL-0004 |
| 8.3.2 | A-8.3.2-02 | syntax | core | A FOR loop written inside the body of another FOR loop may not use the same control variable, so such a program is rejected before it runs. | CTL-0005, CTL-0006 |
| 8.3.2 | A-8.3.2-03 | syntax | core | The variable named by the NEXT that closes a FOR loop must be the same one the FOR line used, so crossed loops (a NEXT naming an outer loop's variable while an inner FOR is still open) are rejected before the program runs, in the main program and in every subprogram. | CTL-0027, CTL-0287, CTL-0288, CTL-0289 |
| 8.3.2 | A-8.3.2-04 | syntax | core | A control transfer from outside a loop may not land on a line inside that loop's for-body or do-body. | CTL-0028, CTL-0029 |
| 8.3.2 | A-ECMA-20 | semantics | core | DO WHILE, DO...LOOP UNTIL with INPUT, DO with EXIT DO, FOR...NEXT, FOR...STEP and a named NEXT all loop as written. | ECMA-0029, ECMA-0030, ECMA-0031, ECMA-0032, ECMA-0033, ECMA-0034 |
| 8.3.3 | A-8.3.3-EX | syntax | core | Every loop example of section 8.3.3 is accepted and behaves as written. | CTL-0030, CTL-0031, CTL-0032, CTL-0033 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-01 | semantics | core | A WHILE exit condition demands leaving the loop when its expression is false, and an UNTIL one when its expression is true. | CTL-0034 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-02 | semantics | core | At a DO line its exit condition is evaluated if present: when it does not demand exit the next line runs, when it does, execution skips past the matching LOOP line; at a LOOP line the condition works the other way, resuming at the DO line unless exit is demanded, in which case execution continues past the LOOP line. | CTL-0035 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-03 | semantics | core | FOR v = a TO b STEP c closed by NEXT v behaves like the spelled-out expansion that stores b and c in hidden per-loop variables, sets v to a, repeats while v has not passed b, and adds c after each round. | CTL-0036 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-04 | semantics | core | The hidden limit and increment variables of a FOR loop belong to that loop alone and cannot be named by the program. | CTL-0037 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-05 | semantics | core | A jump aimed at the FOR line behaves as a jump to the expansion's first assignment, and one aimed at the NEXT line as a jump to its final assignment. | CTL-0038 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-06 | semantics | core | A FOR without STEP adds +1 to the control variable each round. | CTL-0039 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-07 | semantics | core | EXIT DO resumes execution at the line after the LOOP line of the smallest DO loop containing it. | CTL-0040 |
| 8.3.4 | A-8.3.4-08 | semantics | core | EXIT FOR resumes execution at the line after the NEXT line of the smallest FOR loop containing it. | CTL-0041 |
| 8.4.2 | A-8.4.2-01 | syntax | core | The constants in the case-lists of a SELECT block must all be the same type, numeric or string, as the SELECT CASE expression. | CTL-0042, CTL-0043 |
| 8.4.2 | A-8.4.2-02 | syntax | core | The constants and ranges of the case-lists within one SELECT block must not overlap. | CTL-0044, CTL-0045 |
| 8.4.2 | A-8.4.2-03 | syntax | core | A control transfer from outside a structured block may not name a line inside that block, except the IF...THEN line of an if-block or the SELECT line of a select-block. | CTL-0046, CTL-0047, CTL-0048 |
| 8.4.2 | A-8.4.2-04 | syntax | core | A control transfer inside an elseif, else, case or case-else block may not name that block's own header line. | CTL-0049, CTL-0050, CTL-0051, CTL-0052 |
| 8.4.2 | A-8.4.2-TR149 | semantics | core | A case-else-block may be empty (a CASE ELSE line with no block after it): when no case-block matches, the select-block does nothing and execution resumes after END SELECT, without the exception 10004, which is reserved for a select-block with no case-else-block. | CTL-0270, CTL-0271, CTL-0272 |
| 8.4.2 | A-8.4.2-TR152 | syntax | core | The branches of an if-block or select-block (then-block, elseif-block, else-block, case-block, case-else-block, each including its own header line) are blocks in their own right: a control transfer outside one of them, including one inside a sibling branch, may not name a line inside it (its header or its body); a transfer within the same branch, out of the structure, or to the end-if-line or end-select-line stays valid. | CTL-0280, CTL-0281, CTL-0282, CTL-0283, CTL-0284, CTL-0285, CTL-0286 |
| 8.4.2 | A-ECMA-21 | semantics | core | One-line IF with GOSUB, numeric and string targets, IF...ELSE...END IF blocks with ELSEIF, and SELECT CASE with range and IS cases work as written. | ECMA-0035, ECMA-0036, ECMA-0037, ECMA-0038, ECMA-0039 |
| 8.4.3 | A-8.4.3-EX | syntax | core | Every decision-structure example of section 8.4.3 is accepted and behaves as written. | CTL-0053, CTL-0054 |
| 8.4.4 | A-8.4.4-01 | semantics | core | An IF statement with a true condition runs the statement after THEN or jumps to its line number; with a false condition it runs the ELSE statement or jumps to the ELSE line number when present, and otherwise simply continues with the next line. | CTL-0055 |
| 8.4.4 | A-8.4.4-02 | semantics | core | In an if-block an empty branch acts like a remark line; the then-branch runs when its condition is true, otherwise the elseif conditions are tried in order and the first true one enters its branch, otherwise the else-branch runs when present, and leaving any branch resumes after the END IF line. | CTL-0056 |
| 8.4.4 | A-8.4.4-03 | semantics | core | SELECT CASE evaluates its expression and scans the case statements in order until one matches by constant equality, by lying inside a TO range, or by satisfying an IS relation; the rest of that case-block then runs, a non-matching expression runs CASE ELSE when present, and leaving any case block resumes after END SELECT. | CTL-0057 |
| 8.4.5 | E-10004 | exception | core | A SELECT block with no CASE ELSE in which no case-block matches raises the fatal exception 10004. | CTL-0058 |
| 9 | A-9-01 | syntax | core | A routine must be defined or declared on a line before its first call within the program unit, so a function used before its DEF is rejected; defining a routine that is never called is not an error. Internal subprograms are the one relaxation the text allows (A-9.2.2-06). | SEG-0189, SEG-0190 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-01 | semantics | core | The closing line (END PICTURE) of an internal picture is a line of that routine, so a transfer from inside it to that line is valid and takes effect. | SEG-0155 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-03 | syntax | core | A control transfer inside an internal function definition may not name the header line of that function, even if it would never be executed; the program is rejected before it runs. | SEG-0157 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-04 | syntax | core | A control transfer inside an external function definition must not name that function's header line. | SEG-0191 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-05 | syntax | core | A function is defined once: an external one once in the whole program and an internal one once per program unit, and a unit cannot declare or define two functions with the same name. | SEG-0192, SEG-0193 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-06 | syntax | core | An external function must be declared with DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION on a line before its first reference in the same program unit. | SEG-0194, SEG-0195 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-07 | syntax | core | A multi-line internal function must be defined, or declared with DECLARE FUNCTION, before its first reference. | SEG-0196, SEG-0197 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-08 | syntax | core | A single-line DEF function must be defined, or declared with DECLARE DEF, before its first reference. | SEG-0198, SEG-0199 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-09 | syntax | core | A function that refers to itself needs no declaration for that self-reference. | SEG-0200 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-10 | syntax | core | EXIT FUNCTION is valid only inside a function definition. | SEG-0201 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-11 | syntax | core | A multi-line function definition contains at least one LET that assigns to the function's own name. | SEG-0202 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-12 | syntax | core | A function reference supplies exactly as many arguments as the definition has parameters. | SEG-0203, SEG-0204 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-13 | syntax | core | Function arguments match parameters by position and type: a numeric expression for a numeric variable, a string expression for a string variable, and an array of the same kind for a formal array. | SEG-0205, SEG-0206 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-14 | syntax | core | An array argument has one dimension more than the number of commas in the matching formal array. | SEG-0207 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-15 | syntax | core | A formal array of a function has at most three dimensions. | SEG-0208, SEG-0348 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-16 | syntax | core | A numeric argument passed to a function in another program unit requires both units to use the same ARITHMETIC option. | SEG-0209 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-17 | syntax | core | A numeric external function uses the same ARITHMETIC option as the unit that invokes it. | SEG-0210 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-18 | syntax | core | A parameter name appears only once in a function's parameter list. | SEG-0211 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-19 | syntax | core | Function parameters are neither declared nor dimensioned inside the function definition. | SEG-0212 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-20 | syntax | core | A name in DECLARE DEF or DECLARE FUNCTION must be defined in the same program unit by the matching kind of definition: DECLARE DEF requires a one-line DEF and DECLARE FUNCTION requires a multi-line FUNCTION. A program that declares one without defining it, or defines it with the other kind, is rejected when it is loaded, even if the function is never called. | SEG-0213, SEG-0214, SEG-0676, SEG-0677, SEG-0678, SEG-0679, SEG-0680, SEG-0681, SEG-0682 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-21 | syntax | core | A program that declares an external function with DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION and then invokes it without any definition is rejected at load (SEG-0215). | SEG-0215 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-22 | semantics | core | A control transfer outside an internal function definition may name the header line of that function; reaching it has no effect and execution continues at the line after the END FUNCTION. | SEG-0158 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-TR136 | semantics | core | The detached-handler of an internal FUNCTION of the main program may invoke its own FUNCTION (a self-recursive function need not declare itself), with the arguments checked against the parameters of the FUNCTION. | SEG-0521 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-TR137 | semantics | core | A declare-statement written inside a picture-def counts as a declaration of the program-unit of the picture: an EXTERNAL picture, or an internal picture of the main program, may use an external FUNCTION declared with DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION, or a DEF declared with DECLARE DEF, in a lower-numbered line of the picture; a declare-statement that follows the use in the picture does not count and the program is rejected. | SEG-0524, SEG-0525, SEG-0526, SEG-0527 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-TR143 | semantics | core | The detached-handler of the main program, and that of an internal SUB of the main program, may invoke an external FUNCTION that the main program declares with DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION in a lower-numbered line. | SEG-0550 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-TR162 | semantics | core | An internal FUNCTION or DEF (numeric or string) of the main program with the same name as an external FUNCTION takes precedence over it inside the main program and is no longer rejected as a duplicate definition; a unit with DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION of the name uses the external function. DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION Q together with an internal FUNCTION or DEF Q in the same program-unit is still rejected (no more than one function of a name per program-unit). | SEG-0605, SEG-0606, SEG-0607, SEG-0610 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-TR163 | semantics | core | Within an external program-unit, no more than one function of a given name may be defined or declared: two DEF, two FUNCTION, a DEF and a FUNCTION of the same name, or DECLARE EXTERNAL FUNCTION together with a DEF or FUNCTION of the name, are rejected as a duplicate definition, as in the main program. Internal functions of the same name in different program-units are distinct and accepted. | SEG-0611, SEG-0612, SEG-0613, SEG-0614, SEG-0615 |
| 9.1.2 | A-9.1.2-TR170 | semantics | core | Two external FUNCTION definitions of the same name are rejected with E-DUPLICATE-DEFINITION whatever their parameters (none, numeric or string function, used or not). A CALL of a name that is no subprogram (undefined, a detached handler, or a name for which only the string function exists) is rejected with E-SUBPROGRAM-NOT-DEFINED instead of an error that quotes the internal label. | SEG-0660, SEG-0661, SEG-0662, SEG-0663, SEG-0664, SEG-0665 |
| 9.1.2 | A-ECMA-22 | semantics | core | Numeric and string DEF functions, a multi-name function declaration list (FUNCTION a, b$ and EXTERNAL FUNCTION a, b$, ECMA example 21), and an EXTERNAL FUNCTION with SELECT CASE work as written. | ECMA-0041, ECMA-0042, ECMA-0043, ECMA-0044 |
| 9.1.3 | A-9.1.3-01 | syntax | core | Every function definition and declaration shown in the examples of section 9.1.3 is accepted and behaves as written. | SEG-0216, SEG-0217, SEG-0218 |
| 9.1.4.1 | A-9.1.4.1-01 | semantics | core | The arguments of a function reference are evaluated from left to right. | SEG-0219 |
| 9.1.4.1 | A-9.1.4.1-02 | semantics | core | Function arguments are passed by value, so assigning to a parameter inside a function leaves the caller's variable unchanged; this holds for an array argument too (assigning to or redimensioning the formal array leaves the actual array unchanged). | SEG-0220, SEG-0330, SEG-0331, SEG-0345 |
| 9.1.4.1 | A-9.1.4.1-03 | semantics | core | A formal array parameter of a function starts with the same bounds as the actual array, and with a copy of its values. | SEG-0221, SEG-0332, SEG-0346 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-01 | semantics | core | A single-line DEF function evaluates its expression and returns the result as its value. | SEG-0223 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-02 | semantics | core | A multi-line function runs its lines in order until a transfer elsewhere, a fatal exception, CHAIN or STOP, EXIT FUNCTION, or END FUNCTION. | SEG-0224 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-03 | semantics | core | The value of a function is set by LET statements that assign to the function's name. | SEG-0225 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-04 | semantics | core | On exit a function returns the last value assigned to its name during that call. | SEG-0226 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-05 | semantics | core | A length limit after a string function name caps the returned string; without one the ordinary string-variable limit applies. | SEG-0228, SEG-0229 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-06 | semantics | core | EXIT FUNCTION ends the function that contains it. | SEG-0230 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-07 | semantics | core | Reaching END FUNCTION ends the execution of the function. | SEG-0231 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-08 | semantics | core | STOP inside a function ends the whole program. | SEG-0232 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-09 | semantics | core | A function may call itself, directly or through another function. | SEG-0233 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-10 | semantics | core | The lines of a function definition run only when the function is referenced. | SEG-0234 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-11 | semantics | core | Reaching a DEF line during normal flow has no effect and execution continues with the next line. | SEG-0235 |
| 9.1.4.2 | A-9.1.4.2-12 | semantics | core | Reaching the header line of an internal multi-line function during normal flow skips to the line after its END FUNCTION. | SEG-0236 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-01 | semantics | core | A function parameter is local to each invocation and names an object distinct from any same-named variable or array outside the function. | SEG-0237 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-02 | semantics | core | In an external function, every variable and array that is not a parameter is local to each invocation of the function. | SEG-0238 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-03 | semantics | core | In an internal function, variables and arrays that are not parameters belong to the containing program unit, keep their values between calls, and changes remain after the function returns. | SEG-0240 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-04 | semantics | files | A nonzero channel number inside an external function is local to each invocation, and inside an internal function it belongs to the containing program unit. | SEG-0241 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-05 | semantics | files | Channel zero is the same channel in the whole program, in every function. | SEG-0242 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-06 | semantics | files | A file must be assigned to a nonzero channel by OPEN before the channel is used. | SEG-0243 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-07 | semantics | files | Files assigned to channels local to a function are closed when the function exits. | SEG-0244 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-08 | semantics | core | DATA statements inside an external function are local to each invocation of that function. | SEG-0245 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-09 | semantics | core | READ and RESTORE inside an external function use only the DATA statements of that function. | SEG-0246 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-10 | semantics | core | On each invocation of an external function, its DATA pointer is reset to the first datum. | SEG-0247 |
| 9.1.4.3 | A-9.1.4.3-11 | semantics | core | DATA inside an internal function joins the data sequence of the containing unit, and READ and RESTORE there use that whole sequence. | SEG-0248, SEG-0319 |
| 9.1.5 | A-9.1.5-TR90 | exception | core | A string-defined function whose value is longer than its length-max raises fatal exception 1106 and the error is reported on the line of the statement that assigns the value: the DEF line for a one-line DEF, the function-let line for a multi-line FUNCTION, never on line 0. | SEG-0395, SEG-0396 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.1.2-02 | semantics | core | A control transfer outside an internal subprogram may name the header line of that subprogram; reaching it has no effect and execution continues at the line after the END SUB. | SEG-0156 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-01 | syntax | core | EXIT SUB is only valid inside a subprogram definition, so a program that uses it in the main program, in a function, or in a detached handler of the main program is rejected before it runs, even if the statement would never be executed. | SEG-0149, SEG-0150, SEG-0151, EXC-0074 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-02 | syntax | core | A subprogram name may be defined only once in a program unit, and an external subprogram only once in the whole program, so a program with two definitions of the same subprogram name is rejected before it runs. | SEG-0152, SEG-0153 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-03 | syntax | core | A control transfer inside an internal subprogram may not name the header line of that subprogram, even if it would never be executed; the program is rejected before it runs. | SEG-0154 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-04 | syntax | core | A control transfer inside an external subprogram definition must not name that subprogram's header line. | SEG-0249 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-05 | syntax | core | An external subprogram must be declared with DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB on a line before the first CALL that names it in the same program unit: a program that calls it without that declaration, with the declaration after the call, or with the declaration only in another program unit is rejected. | SEG-0185, SEG-0186, SEG-0187, SEG-0188 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-06 | syntax | core | An internal subprogram may be defined, or declared with DECLARE SUB, before its first reference; the text also allows an implementation to accept the reference first, and this one does (SEG-0250 runs a CALL placed before the SUB). | SEG-0250, SEG-0251 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-07 | syntax | core | A subprogram that calls itself needs no declaration for that call. | SEG-0252 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-08 | syntax | core | A CALL supplies exactly as many arguments as the subprogram has parameters. | SEG-0253, SEG-0254 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-09 | syntax | core | CALL arguments match parameters by position and type: expression for a simple variable, array for a formal array, and a channel expression for a channel parameter. | SEG-0255, SEG-0256, SEG-0257 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-10 | syntax | core | An array argument has as many dimensions as the formal array, which is the number of commas plus one. | SEG-0258 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-11 | syntax | core | A numeric argument passed to a subprogram in another program unit requires both units to use the same ARITHMETIC option. | SEG-0259 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-12 | syntax | core | A parameter name appears only once in a subprogram's parameter list. | SEG-0260 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-13 | syntax | core | Subprogram parameters are neither declared nor dimensioned inside the subprogram definition. | SEG-0261 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-14 | syntax | files | Channel number zero cannot be used as a subprogram parameter. | SEG-0262 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-15 | syntax | core | A name in DECLARE SUB must be defined in the same program unit by an internal subprogram. | SEG-0263 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-16 | syntax | core | A name in DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB must be defined by an external subprogram elsewhere in the program. | SEG-0264 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-17 | syntax | core | No more than one subprogram of a given name, internal or external, is declared or defined in a program unit: a second DECLARE of the same subprogram, or a DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB for a name that the unit also defines as an internal SUB, is rejected before the program runs. | SEG-0315, SEG-0316, SEG-0317 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-18 | semantics | core | A subprogram need not declare itself: a CALL that names the subprogram from inside its own external definition loads and runs without any DECLARE of that name in that program unit. | SEG-0323 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR134 | semantics | core | The detached-handler of an EXTERNAL unit (SUB or FUNCTION) or of an internal SUB of such a unit is part of that program-unit: a CALL in it to an external SUB needs a DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB of the SUB in a lower-numbered line of the same program-unit, and the declare-statements of the main program do not count. The program is rejected when only the main program declares the SUB. The SUB that owns the handler is exempt from this declaration when it calls itself (self-recursion, l.4534-4537; A-9.2.2-TR136). | SEG-0515, SEG-0516, SEG-0517, SEG-0518, SEG-0519 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR136 | semantics | core | The detached-handler of an internal SUB of the main program may CALL its own SUB (a self-recursive subprogram need not declare itself): the CALL is accepted, with the arguments checked against the parameters of the SUB, and the handler runs when the exception occurs in the SUB. | SEG-0520 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR136B | semantics | core | Each program-unit checks the declare-statements of external SUBs against its own lines: when several EXTERNAL units declare the same SUB, the CALL in the detached-handler of each one is accepted if its own unit declares the SUB in a lower-numbered line, whatever the line of the declare-statement of another unit; it is rejected if its own unit does not declare it, even if another unit does. | SEG-0522, SEG-0523 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR137 | semantics | core | An EXTERNAL picture may CALL an external SUB that it declares with DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB in a lower-numbered line of the picture, in its body and in its detached-handler; the declare-statements of the main program do not count for the picture, which is rejected when it declares nothing. | SEG-0528, SEG-0529, SEG-0530 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR143 | semantics | core | A CALL in the detached-handler of the main program, or of an internal SUB of the main program, is checked against the declare-statement of the main program even when another program-unit declares the same SUB at a higher line; a SUB declared only by another unit is rejected. | SEG-0551, SEG-0552 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR162 | semantics | core | An internal SUB of the main program with the same name as an external SUB or PICTURE takes precedence over it, for the CALLs of the main program (also from its handlers, from other internal SUBs of the main, with DECLARE SUB and in recursion): the internal SUB is called. A unit that declares the external SUB with DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB calls the external one, whichever unit comes first in the text; DRAW of the external picture does not run the internal SUB. DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB Q together with an internal SUB Q in the same program-unit is still rejected (two subprograms of the name). | SEG-0600, SEG-0601, SEG-0602, SEG-0603, SEG-0604, SEG-0608, SEG-0609 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR164 | semantics | core | SUB and PICTURE are different classes of routine. A CALL names a subprogram and a DRAW names a picture: a CALL of an internal PICTURE (of the main or of a unit), or a DRAW of an internal SUB or of an external SUB declared with DECLARE EXTERNAL SUB, is rejected when the program is loaded instead of running the routine of the other class. An internal SUB of the main program and an external PICTURE of the same name coexist: CALL runs the SUB and DRAW draws the external picture. | SEG-0616, SEG-0617, SEG-0618, SEG-0619, SEG-0620, SEG-0627, SEG-0628 |
| 9.2.2 | A-9.2.2-TR171 | semantics | core | A channel-number formal parameter (SUB W(#2), PICTURE P(#2)) only accepts a channel-expression (#n, #K, #K + 1) as argument, and a numeric parameter does not accept a channel-expression: a number or a numeric variable passed to a channel-number parameter, a string passed to it, or a channel-expression passed to a numeric parameter is rejected with E-TYPE-MISMATCH when the program is loaded, for external and internal SUBs and for pictures called with DRAW. The legal passing of channels is unchanged. | SEG-0666, SEG-0667, SEG-0668, SEG-0669, SEG-0670, SEG-0671, SEG-0672, SEG-0673 |
| 9.2.2 | A-ECMA-23 | semantics | core | Internal and external SUBprograms (with formal arrays, a string and a channel parameter) called with computed arguments work as written. | ECMA-0045, ECMA-0046, ECMA-0047 |
| 9.2.3 | A-9.2.3-01 | syntax | core | Every subprogram definition, declaration and call shown in the examples of section 9.2.3 is accepted and behaves as written. | SEG-0265, SEG-0266 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-01 | semantics | core | A CALL transfers control to the named subprogram, whose body runs before the program continues. | SEG-0146 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-02 | semantics | core | A subprogram body runs in order until a transfer elsewhere, a fatal exception, CHAIN, STOP, EXIT SUB, or END SUB ends it. | SEG-0267 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-03 | semantics | core | EXIT SUB ends the innermost subprogram that contains it. | SEG-0268 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-04 | semantics | core | When a subprogram finishes, execution resumes on the line after the CALL that started it. | SEG-0146 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-05 | semantics | core | STOP inside a subprogram ends the whole program. | SEG-0269 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-06 | semantics | core | A subprogram may call itself, directly or through another procedure. | SEG-0270 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-07 | semantics | core | The lines of a subprogram definition run only when a CALL references it. | SEG-0271 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-08 | semantics | core | Reaching the header line of an internal subprogram during normal flow skips to the line after its END SUB. | SEG-0272 |
| 9.2.4 | A-9.2.4-TR132 | semantics | core | A variable that is a procedure-argument is passed by reference also when the call is made from the body of an EXTERNAL unit and the variable is local to that unit: assigning the procedure-parameter in the internal SUB assigns the variable. A parameter of an EXTERNAL unit whose argument is a literal or an expression is a value local to the invocation of the unit: an internal SUB of the unit sees it and assigns it, and the unit sees the assignment afterwards. | SEG-0511, SEG-0512, SEG-0513, SEG-0514 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-01 | semantics | core | An array element given as a subprogram argument is passed by reference, so assigning to the parameter changes the element. | SEG-0142, SEG-0159, SEG-0160, SEG-0161, SEG-0162, SEG-0163, SEG-0164, SEG-0165, SEG-0166 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-02 | semantics | core | A subprogram argument that is a parenthesized variable or array element is an expression: its value is copied to a local location, so assigning to the parameter leaves the caller's variable unchanged. | SEG-0141, SEG-0143, SEG-0144, SEG-0145 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-03 | semantics | core | A simple variable given without parentheses as a subprogram argument is passed by reference, so assigning to the parameter changes the variable. | SEG-0146 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-04 | semantics | core | On a CALL the arguments are matched with the parameters from left to right. | SEG-0273 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-05 | semantics | core | A string variable given without a substring qualifier as a CALL argument is passed by reference, so assigning to the parameter changes the variable. | SEG-0274 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-06 | semantics | core | A string variable with a substring qualifier, being an expression, is passed by value. | SEG-0168, SEG-0169 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-07 | semantics | core | The subscripts of an array element passed as an argument are evaluated once at each entry to the subprogram. | SEG-0167 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-08 | semantics | core | Argument expressions of a CALL are evaluated from left to right. | SEG-0275 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-09 | semantics | core | A formal array parameter stands for the caller's array: reading, assigning and redimensioning it inside the subprogram act on that array. | SEG-0276, SEG-0277 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-10 | semantics | core | A formal array parameter starts with the same bounds as the actual array. | SEG-0278 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-11 | semantics | core | A string parameter passed by reference has the maximum length of its argument; for a string-array parameter, MAXLEN of the formal is that of the actual array. | SEG-0182, SEG-0183, SEG-0184, SEG-0333 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-12 | semantics | files | A channel expression passed to a subprogram is evaluated once on entry and the resulting channel is used for every reference to the parameter. | SEG-0280, SEG-0284, SEG-0322, SEG-0683 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-13 | semantics | files | The file on a passed channel keeps its attributes on entry, and changes made to it inside the subprogram take effect at once through any channel number and persist after exit. | SEG-0281 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-14 | semantics | files | A file need not be open on a channel passed to a subprogram, and an OPEN inside the subprogram stays in effect after it exits. | SEG-0282, SEG-0283 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-15 | semantics | core | Every statement that assigns to a variable (READ, INPUT, LINE INPUT, FOR, ASK, file READ, substring assignment) acts on the location the parameter denotes: the caller's variable or array element when it was passed by reference. | SEG-0172, SEG-0173, SEG-0174, SEG-0176, SEG-0177, SEG-0178, SEG-0179, SEG-0180, SEG-0181 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-16 | semantics | core | When the argument is an expression, assignments of any kind to the parameter act on a location local to the invocation, which later reads of the parameter see, and leave the caller's variable unchanged. | SEG-0175 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-17 | semantics | core | A parameter received by value is a variable local to the invocation of an internal or external SUB or FUNCTION, and a GOSUB/RETURN inside the procedure does not isolate it: an assignment made to it in the subroutine is still seen after RETURN, for numeric and string parameters and with nested GOSUB. | SEG-0334 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-TR142 | semantics | core | Arguments are evaluated left to right and a variable argument is passed by reference even when a later argument of the same CALL or DRAW calls a user function (DEF, internal or external FUNCTION): the parameter stays bound to the variable, reads its value and an assignment to the parameter reaches the variable. | SEG-0560 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-TR146 | semantics | core | A GOSUB subroutine does not create a scope: a by-value parameter of a CALL, a FUNCTION or a DEF invoked inside it (also nested, from ON GOSUB, or inside an EXTERNAL SUB) takes the value of its argument and the routine reads it, exactly as outside the subroutine. | SEG-0570, SEG-0571, SEG-0572 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-TR146B | semantics | core | An array is passed by reference to an internal or EXTERNAL SUB or FUNCTION whose name contains one or more underlines, also when the formal array name contains underlines: the routine reads and assigns the elements of the actual array. | SEG-0573, SEG-0574, SEG-0575 |
| 9.2.4.1 | A-9.2.4.1-TR172 | semantics | core | In CALL S(Q(1)) with Q an array parameter of the unit that has the name of an external FUNCTION the unit does not declare, Q(1) is an element of the array and is passed by reference (the assignment of S to its parameter reaches the array), as with a local array. A function declared or defined in the unit is still called and its value passed by value. | SEG-0674, SEG-0675 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-01 | semantics | core | A parameter passed by value is local to each invocation and names an object distinct from any same-named variable outside. | SEG-0285 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-02 | semantics | core | A parameter passed by reference has a name local to each invocation, but it names the same object as the argument. | SEG-0286 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-03 | semantics | core | In an external subprogram, every variable and array that is not a parameter is local to each invocation. | SEG-0287 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-04 | semantics | core | In an internal subprogram, variables and arrays that are not parameters belong to the containing program unit, keep their values between calls, and changes remain after the subprogram returns. | SEG-0289 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-05 | semantics | files | A nonzero channel number inside an external subprogram is local to each invocation, and inside an internal subprogram it belongs to the containing program unit. | SEG-0290 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-06 | semantics | files | Channel zero is the same channel in the whole program, in every subprogram. | SEG-0291 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-07 | semantics | files | A file must be assigned to a nonzero channel by OPEN before the channel is used. | SEG-0292 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-08 | semantics | files | Files assigned to channels local to a subprogram are closed when the subprogram exits. | SEG-0293 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-09 | semantics | core | DATA statements inside an external subprogram are local to each invocation of it. | SEG-0294 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-10 | semantics | core | READ and RESTORE inside an external subprogram use only the DATA statements of that subprogram. | SEG-0295 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-11 | semantics | core | On each invocation of an external subprogram, its DATA pointer is reset to the first datum. | SEG-0296 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-113 | semantics | core | In an external subprogram, the variables that are not parameters are local to the invocation and distinct from the variables of the same name outside; whether the target of READ, INPUT or LINE INPUT is a string variable, its length-max and its fixed-point-size are decided from the name of the LOCAL variable, never from a global variable of the main program that happens to share its position in the symbol table, so a string local with numeric globals (and the reverse) is read without a spurious 8101 or 8102. | SEG-0498 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-12 | semantics | core | DATA inside an internal subprogram joins the data sequence of the containing unit, and READ and RESTORE there use that whole sequence. | SEG-0297, SEG-0318 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR116 | semantics | core | The parameters of an EXTERNAL SUB or FUNCTION are names of that program unit, so its internal SUBs and FUNCTIONs and the DEFs of its body read and assign them (an assignment reaches the actual argument, which is passed by reference; an array parameter is used with its elements and bounds); a parameter of the internal routine itself with the same name hides the unit parameter. | SEG-0499, SEG-0500, ARR-0311 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR117 | semantics | core | The arrays that an internal SUB or FUNCTION of an EXTERNAL unit dimensions or declares belong to the unit and to each invocation of it: they exist, with their bounds and without the values of a previous invocation, in the first call of the unit and in every later one, and the internal routine and the body of the unit see the same array. | ARR-0312, ARR-0313 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR141 | semantics | core | The name of a parameter is local to each invocation of an internal SUB, also in recursion: when the outermost invocation of a recursive internal SUB is bound by reference to a variable of the caller, the nested invocations whose argument is an expression evaluate it on each entry and read their own parameter, not the variable bound by the first call; only the outermost invocation assigns to that variable. | SEG-0540, SEG-0541, SEG-0542 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR142 | semantics | core | A local variable of an external SUB, FUNCTION or PICTURE that has not been assigned yet and is passed by reference to another subprogram is that same local variable of the invocation: the called subprogram assigns it, and the caller reads the value afterwards without a warning and without touching any other variable of the unit, including in recursion with output parameters. | SEG-0561, SEG-0562 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR147A | semantics | core | An internal SUB or FUNCTION called from another internal routine sees, under the name of the formal array of the caller, the array of the program-unit that contains both (not the actual array of the caller's invocation): reads and assignments in the callee reach the unit array, also inside an external SUB and when the caller is an internal FUNCTION. | SEG-0580, SEG-0581, SEG-0582, SEG-0583 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR147B | semantics | core | A variable of an external SUB, FUNCTION or PICTURE that has not been assigned yet and is passed by reference from an internal routine of that unit is the variable of the invocation of the unit: the called subprogram assigns it (numeric or string), the unit reads the value afterwards, also in recursion with an output parameter. | SEG-0584, SEG-0585, SEG-0586 |
| 9.2.4.2 | A-9.2.4.2-TR150 | semantics | core | An array that an external SUB or PICTURE declares for itself is local to each invocation and is distinct from an array outside with the same name, also when that outside array is the actual argument of the very CALL or DRAW (numeric or string arrays, call-site in the main program, in an internal routine or in a GOSUB routine, GOSUB inside the unit, recursion with the local passed down). | SEG-0590, SEG-0591, SEG-0592, SEG-0593, SEG-0594, SEG-0595 |
| 9.2.6 | A-9.2.6-01 | semantics | core | When two names refer to the same object because of by-reference parameters, a change made through one name is seen at once through the other, so the aliasing example of section 9.2.6 never prints its message. | SEG-0298 |
| 9.3.2 | A-9.3.2-01 | syntax | core | The arguments of CHAIN WITH are matched with the parameters of the chained program's header line by the same count and type rules as function arguments. | SEG-0299 |
| 9.3.2 | A-ECMA-24 | semantics | core | CHAIN with a literal or a string expression and a WITH list is accepted; chaining to an unavailable program raises 10005. | ECMA-0048, ECMA-0049 |
| 9.3.3 | A-9.3.3-01 | syntax | core | Both CHAIN forms shown in the examples of section 9.3.3 are accepted. | SEG-0300, SEG-0301 |
| 9.3.4 | A-9.3.4-01 | semantics | core | CHAIN ends the running program, closes every file and starts the designated program. | SEG-0302 |
| 9.3.4 | A-9.3.4-02 | semantics | core | CHAIN WITH arguments are evaluated and passed by value to the parameters in the chained program's header line. | SEG-0314 |
| 9.3.4 | A-9.3.4-03 | semantics | core | A formal array in the chained program takes the bounds of the actual array, as for function parameters. | SEG-0303 |
| 9.3.4 | A-9.3.4-04 | semantics | core | A string array can be passed by CHAIN WITH to a formal string-array of the program-name-line (1, 2 or 3 dimensions, mixed with scalar and numeric-array parameters); the formal takes the bounds of the actual and the default maximum string length. | SEG-0390, SEG-0391, SEG-0392 |
| 9.3.5 | A-9.3.5-01 | semantics | core | CHAIN passing numeric parameters between two FIXED units with different fixed-point sizes executes without exception: only the ARITHMETIC type must agree (15.2.2 l.12354-12357, 'both be DECIMAL or NATIVE or FIXED'), not the precision; the program-name-line parameters do not trigger the ordering rule of 15.1.2 l.12145-12148 (agreed interpretation of 15.2.2). | SEG-0324 |
| 9.3.5 | E-10005 | exception | core | CHAIN to a program that is not available raises the fatal exception 10005, which a handler can intercept; without a handler the program stops at the CHAIN statement. | SEG-0147, SEG-0148 |
| 9.3.5 | E-4301 | exception | core | CHAIN whose arguments differ in number or type from the chained program's parameters, or to a program without a parameter list, ends the run with fatal exception 4301. | SEG-0307, SEG-0308, SEG-0309, SEG-0393 |
| 9.3.5 | E-4302 | exception | core | CHAIN with an array argument whose dimension count differs from its formal array ends the run with fatal exception 4302. | SEG-0310, SEG-0313, SEG-0394 |
| 9.3.5 | E-4303 | exception | core | CHAIN passing numeric parameters between program-units whose ARITHMETIC options differ in type (DECIMAL vs NATIVE vs FIXED; a unit without an ARITHMETIC option is DECIMAL, 5.6.4 l.2234-2236) ends the run with fatal exception 4303; with no numeric parameters passed (no WITH, or only string arguments) there is no 4303 even if the ARITHMETIC types differ (9.3.5 l.4918-4920: only when numeric parameters are passed). | SEG-0311, SEG-0312, SEG-0325, SEG-0326, SEG-0327, SEG-0328, SEG-0329 |
| 10.1 | E-1506 | exception | core | An implementation may raise nonfatal exception 1506 for a numeric DATA underflow (supply zero and continue), so a handler can intercept it. | PRT-0025, PRT-0150 |
| 10.1.2 | A-10.1.2-01 | syntax | core | An IF MISSING recovery of EXIT DO (or EXIT FOR) on a READ is only valid inside a DO (or FOR) loop, so otherwise the program is rejected before it runs. | PRT-0003 |
| 10.1.2 | A-10.1.2-02 | syntax | core | A line number after RESTORE must point at a line that holds a DATA statement; any other target is rejected before the program runs. | PRT-0009 |
| 10.1.2 | A-10.1.2-TR118 | semantics | core | The body of a detached-handler is part of the program unit that contains it, and RESTORE is not a control-transfer: RESTORE n may name a DATA line inside a detached-handler of the unit (from the main program, from the when-block that uses the handler, from an internal routine or from the body of an EXTERNAL unit); a RESTORE n that names a DATA line inside a handler of another program unit is still rejected before the program runs. | PRT-0309, PRT-0311 |
| 10.1.2 | A-10.1.2-TR154 | syntax | core | The line-number of an io-recovery (IF MISSING THEN n, IF THERE THEN n) is the line of a control-transfer (8.2.2 prod. 1) and obeys the same scope rules as GOTO: from outside it may not name a line inside an if-block branch, select-block case, for-body, do-body, protection-block (other than its when-line), exception-handler or the header line of its own external subprogram, nor may it jump between sibling branches; jumps within the same branch, out of a structure or to a line of the top level of the same program unit stay valid. | PRT-0390, PRT-0391, PRT-0392, PRT-0393, PRT-0394, PRT-0395, PRT-0396, FIL-0490, FIL-0491 |
| 10.1.2 | A-ECMA-25 | semantics | core | READ with IF MISSING, RESTORE and RESTORE to a line, and DATA with numeric and quoted-string items behave as written; an elided READ item is rejected (known deviation). | ECMA-0050, ECMA-0051, ECMA-0052, ECMA-0053, ECMA-0054 |
| 10.1.3 | A-10.1.3-EX | semantics | core | Every READ, IF MISSING and RESTORE form shown in the examples of section 10.1.3 is accepted and behaves as written. | PRT-0010 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-01 | semantics | core | All DATA statements of a program unit form a single data sequence in textual order, and reaching a DATA line at run time just moves execution to the next line. | PRT-0011 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-02 | semantics | core | A READ assigns the listed variables, left to right, from the data sequence of its unit through a pointer that starts at the first datum and steps past each datum consumed. | PRT-0012 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-03 | semantics | core | Reading past the end of the data sequence raises an exception unless the READ carries IF MISSING; then the chosen action runs: EXIT DO or EXIT FOR behaves normally, and a line number transfers execution to that line. | PRT-0013, PRT-0014, PRT-0015 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-04 | semantics | core | Each datum must match its variable's type: numeric constants for numeric variables, string constants or unquoted strings for string variables; an unquoted string that also parses as a number may fill either kind. | PRT-0016 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-05 | semantics | core | A numeric datum that underflows while being evaluated is stored as zero. | PRT-0017 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-06 | semantics | core | Subscripts and substring qualifiers in a READ list are worked out only after the variables to their left already received their values. | PRT-0018 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-07 | semantics | core | RESTORE rewinds the data pointer of its unit to the first datum, or, with a line number, to the first datum of that DATA line, so the next READ starts there. | PRT-0019 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-08 | semantics | core | The textual order of the data sequence of a program unit also interleaves the DATA statements of its internal subprograms and internal functions by line position; they are not appended after the data of the main body. | SEG-0318, SEG-0319 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-TR109 | semantics | core | The DATA of an internal routine is part of the data sequence of its program unit, and RESTORE is not a control-transfer: RESTORE n may name a DATA line of any internal routine of the unit (from the main, from another routine, or from the body of an EXTERNAL unit), and READ in the routine reads the whole sequence; a RESTORE n that names a line of another program unit is still rejected before the program runs. | PRT-0306, PRT-0308 |
| 10.1.4 | A-10.1.4-TR122 | semantics | core | The data-statements of a detached-handler belong to the data sequence of the program unit that contains the handler, in line order with the other data-statements of that unit: in an EXTERNAL unit, READ reads the DATA of its handler, each invocation of the unit starts at the first datum of its own sequence, and neither the main program nor another unit sees it. | PRT-0312, PRT-0313 |
| 10.1.5 | A-10.1.5-EXC | exception | core | Assigning a datum that is not a numeric constant to a numeric variable in a READ raises fatal exception 8101 (the Table 9 entry is covered by E-8101). | PRT-0020 |
| 10.1.5 | E-1006 | exception | core | An overflow while evaluating a numeric datum during READ or MAT READ raises fatal exception 1006. | PRT-0023, PRT-0210, PRT-0211 |
| 10.1.5 | E-1053 | exception | core | Storing a datum into a string variable or string-array element when it does not fit raises fatal exception 1053 during READ or MAT READ, also when the target is a substring of a variable or array element (10.1.4 l.5038-5041) or a by-reference string parameter whose argument has a smaller length-max (9.2.4.1 l.4679-4682), or an element of a string array with a length-max, or a whole such array in MAT READ (10.5.5 l.6103-6104). | PRT-0024, PRT-0170, SEG-0361, SEG-0370, SEG-0380 |
| 10.1.5 | E-8001 | exception | core | Reading beyond the end of the data sequence with no IF MISSING recovery raises fatal exception 8001, for READ and for MAT READ alike; a handler can intercept it. | PRT-0021, PRT-0022, PRT-0114 |
